item.title: Observation of Antichiral Hinge States in a Three-dimensional Gyromagnetic Photonic Crystal
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77286-6

This work reports the observation of antichiral hinge states in a 3D gyromagnetic photonic crystal. Extending antichirality to higher-order topology, it reveals a topological semimetal with co-propagating transport along parallel hinges.

item.title: A conserved small RNA-generating gene cluster undergoes sequence diversification and contributes to plant immunity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77164-1

Here the authors reveal a conserved small RNA-producing gene cluster that undergoes sequence diversification, driving a co-evolutionary arms race with pathogens. This native innate immunity offers new opportunities to engineer disease resistance in plants.

item.title: Unveiling non-Hermitian band structures with non-Bloch supercells
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77152-5

Non-Hermitian band structures enable unusual phenomena but remain difficult to map beyond one dimension. Here, the authors develop a general non-Bloch supercell framework to resolve complex momentum, energy, eigenstates, and topology, demonstrated in one- and two-dimensional acoustic crystals.

item.title: Bi-directional highways and super-seeder tissues underpin parasite dissemination in experimental Leishmania donovani infection
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77072-4

Ecological analysis of murine Leishmania donovani infection reveals complex parasite within-host dynamics, with super-seeder sites fuelling dissemination between skin and viscera, and with key connections malleable after further immune perturbation.

item.title: How coastal resilience emerges
item.description:
Representative article figure (not a graphical abstract)

Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76127-w

As climate change accelerates and pressures on coastal systems intensify, understanding coastal resilience is becoming as important as understanding the hazards themselves.

item.title: Stabilization of charged domains in ferroelectric BiFeO<sub>3</sub> nanoneedles
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76259-z

The authors propose a top down strategy of modifying the surface boundary conditions in a BiFeO3 nanoneedle sample through ion milling. Surface curvature gradients and terminations induce charge compensation and ferroeleastic effects that facilitate charged domain wall stabilization.

item.title: Socio-economic value of data-driven eruption forecasts to balance false alarms against catastrophic loss
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77242-4

Volcanic disasters cause widespread economic damage. Here, the authors examine the potential economic value of precautionary action compared to losses finding that losses could be reduced 30-90% even with false alarms.

item.title: Mechanical flexibility and pressure-activated emission in room-temperature phosphorescent organic crystals
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77244-2

Folded molecular geometry enables mechanically flexible organic crystals with pressure-activated phosphorescence and reveals how the proportion of ¹(n, π*) character affects spin–orbit coupling.

item.title: A bipartite glucan synthase-remodeler module organizes branched glucan assembly in the fungal cell wall
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 26 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76987-2

Fungal cell walls require glucan polymers to be synthesized and remodeled. Here, authors identify a synthase-remodeler pair that works together to build branched β-glucan and shape cell wall architecture.

item.title: Combinatorial group testing for efficient scaling across biological applications
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77055-5

Combinatorial group testing can reduce experimental costs but remains challenging to apply due to its complexity and the lack of implementation tools. Here, the authors present PoolPy, a complete combinatorial group testing framework, enabling up to 93% cost reduction across biological assays.

item.title: Redox-stratified macromolecule degradation supports microbial survival in the oligotrophic Kermadec Trench sediments
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77249-x

Understanding how microbes survive in the crushing pressure and nutrient-poor conditions of the deepest ocean has remained a major challenge. This study reveals that Kermadec Trench microbes thrive by recycling organic matter and flexibly switching energy-generation pathways.

item.title: Unc-51 like kinase 3 (ULK3) contributes to autophagy and cell survival in multiple myeloma
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76711-0

Autophagy-related mechanisms in multiple myeloma (MM) remains to be understood. Here the authors find that ULK3 contributes to autophagy and supports MM cell survival, calling for future development of more selective ULK3-directed therapies.

item.title: Dual-phase engineering of CF<sub>x</sub> electrode and interphase enables low-temperature Li||CF<sub>x</sub> batteries
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76513-4

Li||CFx batteries exhibit severe low-temperature degradation owing to insulating CFx electrodes and sluggish Li+ kinetics. The authors propose a dual-modification strategy combining carbon-coated porous CFx cathodes with an electrolyte-derived interphase, which accelerates Li+ transport and boosts performance at low temperatures.

item.title: Quantifying replication fidelity of unnatural base pairs using nanopore sequencing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76964-9

Expanded DNA alphabets with more than 4 letters can be replicated by polymerases, but with higher error rates than standard DNA. Here the authors develop a high-throughput sequencing approach to quantify the replication fidelity of unnatural base pairs.

item.title: BRANCHED1 acts as a rheostat of Nuclear Factor Y-dependent epigenetic regulation in axillary bud development
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77029-7

Shoot branching plasticity is largely regulated by BRC1. The authors show that BRC1 acts as a dose-dependent rheostat, modulating NF-Y-mediated chromatin looping and H3K27me3 demethylation at floral organ development genes to fine-tune axillary bud activity.

item.title: Protein entanglement misfolding influences whether proteins undergo proteasomal degradation or persist in near-native misfolded states
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76875-9

Protein entanglements can generate long-lived misfolded states, but their cellular fate is poorly understood. Here, the authors combine proteomics and simulations to show that entanglement misfolding promotes proteasomal degradation, while soluble, near-native misfolded proteins escape degradation.

item.title: Ectoderm tensile stress controls mesoderm internalization during embryo gastrulation
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77010-4

The biomechanical basis for tissue folding during morphogenesis remains incompletely understood. Here they show that precisely balanced mechanical tension in tissues surrounding the future mesoderm is essential for its internalization during fruit fly gastrulation.

item.title: Substrate curvature and stiffness equivalence in governing cell mechanosensing
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76866-w

This study reveals how cells translate substrate stiffness and curvature into biological responses through focal adhesion tilting, uncovering a mechanical equivalence that opens new routes for designing cell-instructive biomaterials.

item.title: The predicted interactome of the human mitochondrial proteome
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77112-z

The molecular function of many mitochondrial proteins remains unknown. Here, the authors present MitoMatch, an AlphaFold Multimer-based compendium of mitochondrial protein interactions that links orphan proteins to known pathways, defines the CoQ metabolon, and reveals the role of COA4 in copper delivery to cytochrome c oxidase.

item.title: Role of natural halogen chemistry on the evolution of global stratospheric ozone depletion
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76600-6

Halogens from natural sources account for a substantial fraction of stratospheric ozone depletion, contributing up to half of recent lower-stratospheric ozone loss and delaying Antarctic ozone recovery by several decades.

item.title: Homo-metal-element mediated surface modification of sapphire for robust epitaxy of wafer-scale single-crystalline 2D semiconductors
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77131-w

The wafer-scale growth of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides is desired for their electronic applications. Here, the authors report a surface modification strategy of commercial sapphire substrates to grow wafer-scale monolayer WS2 or MoS2 single crystals, showing their application for high-performance transistors arrays.

item.title: Amide synthesis via molecular shuffling of carboxylic acids
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77092-0

The amide bond represents the most fundamental functional group in chemistry and biology. Herein, the authors report an approach to amide synthesis that relies on molecular shuffling of carboxylic acid functional group.

item.title: Optimising antibiotic switching via forecasting of patient physiology
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76715-w

The authors present a decision support system that forecasts patients’ vital signs to identify those ready to switch from intravenous to oral antibiotics. Clinical criteria are applied to the forecasts to rank patients for stewardship review.

item.title: Exosomal export of activated CASPASE-8 is linked to the prevention of TNF-induced cytotoxicity
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-75544-1

The ESCRT machinery and the chaperone HSC70 package activated CASP8 into intralumenal vesicles preventing TNF-induced apoptosis. Microbial effector proteins interfere with this detoxification mechanism and sensitize cells to TNF cytotoxicity.

item.title: Smart and sustainable production of fertilizer by electrochromic self-perception recovery of ammonium from wastewater
item.description:
Nature Communications, Published online: 25 August 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-76968-5

The authors develop an electrochromic self-perception recovery system that integrates electrochromism-based sensing, predictive modelling and automatic control. This system enables smart ammonium recovery from wastewater and converts it into liquid fertilizer.
